correctness.rationale: Using the actual two-size odd-partition signed coefficient identity of Merca, for n=2^t m (m odd) the normalized coefficient equals r_t - lambda(m)/(4(2^{t+1}-1)sigma(m)). Positive lambda corresponds to sums of two squares by the prime-factor criterion. If t>=1, a different limiting atom would force lambda/sigma>2; if t=0, the 2-adic valuation equality for lambda(m),sigma(m) contradicts an even numerator 2/C_s. Therefore representable indices are outside the discrete limiting support. Every nonempty valuation layer contains n=2^t (sum of two squares), so the finite empirical atom masses are each at most 2^{-t-1}; the entire positive mass off support equals B(N)/N. TV is exactly that value for all N>=1, and Landau--Ramanujan gives the sharp K/sqrt(log N) asymptotic. Independent rational re-enumeration yielded B(256)=97 and TV=97/256; the finite check supplements the universal parity argument.
